surveyed.source: Vertex average of the BAG 0363100012165685 ring (RD, PDOK BAG WFS, CC0); massing is one prism per 3DBAG LoD2.2 roof piece of that pand (CC BY 4.0), each snapped to the floor band that forms its roof edge, in native east/south metres (scripts/landmarks/vijzelstraat-prepare.ts). Band levels, bay axes, the colonnade, the Kerkstraat passage (OSM w34955694) and its void measured on the rectified Gemeente Amsterdam panorama recording_2025-06-16_06-42-40_01588 (20 px/m, CC BY 4.0); see scripts/landmarks/vijzelbank-inventory.json and vijzelbank-elevations.json.

attribution.title: Prins en Keizer, the former ABN bank at Vijzelstraat 66-80 (M.F. Duintjer with J. Trapman, 1969-1973; municipal monument)
attribution.author: Map Recall
attribution.modifications: Original texture-free flat-colour geometry on 3DBAG LoD2.2 roof pieces (CC BY 4.0) and the BAG footprint (CC0): dark floor-edge bands round every terrace, white fins on the bay axes, the white colonnade, the Kerkstraat passage with its double-height void and walkway, fire escapes and terrace railings, read for proportion and tone from Gemeente Amsterdam panoramas (CC BY 4.0) and Wikimedia Commons photographs by Ceescamel (CC BY-SA 4.0) and Rudolphous (CC BY-SA 3.0 nl). Names and dates: Wikipedia nl 'Vijzelbank' (CC BY-SA 4.0) and the municipal monument register. No pixels or meshes imported.

throughPassages.evidence: Kerkstraat building passage (OSM w34955694, tunnel=building_passage) under the block from the Vijzelstraat to the west face, 10.2 m between the gallery piers, seen in panorama recording_2025-06-16_06-42-40_01588 (2025) and its aimed view; Wikipedia nl 'Vijzelbank' (the Kerkstraat was built over).

The public gallery ('voetgangersgalerij met winkels en horeca', Wikipedia nl 'Vijzelbank') runs the whole Vijzelstraat front behind the white piers and is open at both canal ends: panoramas recording_2025-06-16_06-42-40_01588 (front, 2025) and TMX7316010203-002619_pano_0015_000144 (Keizersgracht corner, 2022), Commons File:Vijzelstraat_66-80.jpg (Prinsengracht corner, 2019).
